claim: In continuous robotic breast-ultrasound scanning, smooth path optimization plus static force-strain regression and image-confidence feedback maintained image confidence comparable to higher constant-force settings while lowering desired force on three phantoms; the study does not show whether richer contact state or constrained impedance optimization would improve outcomes further.
epistemic_status: Performance statements are author-reported phantom results; the unresolved need for richer representation and optimal impedance is an inference from the documented method and comparison scope.
problem_and_setting: The paper addresses path smoothness, safe contact regulation, and image quality in robotic breast ultrasound, where deformation and internal structure vary and image-only feedback may not ensure stable force.
method_or_mechanism: DO-ACDC optimizes anti-radial path points and normals for acceleration continuity and low deviation. CFS-DFP predicts desired force from a static force-strain regression fitted by 1 mm/s compressions, while UIC-DFU updates desired force from ultrasound-image confidence between path points.
content_summary: Experiments used a UR5, a force/torque sensor, two silicone phantoms, and a hydrogel-core phantom with silicone skin. DO-ACDC improved angle-increment statistics. Variable desired-force control was compared with 8 N, 6 N, and 3 N constant references and reportedly achieved comparable confidence with lower force. Validation was limited to phantoms and did not compare contact-model classes or constrained impedance policies.
synthesis_role: Direct application evidence that continuous soft scanning benefits from spatially varying contact-aware force regulation, while showing that a simple static representation can be a strong baseline against which richer contact models must earn their complexity.
development_link: A richer model should be compared against this static force-strain plus image-feedback baseline on held-out materials, geometries, speeds, and contact histories; it is justified only if it changes selected impedance actions or improves force, deformation, safety, trajectory, or image outcomes.

evidence.finding: The system combines path smoothing, force-strain desired-force prediction, and image-confidence force updating.
DO-ACDC reduced mean absolute angle increment and its dispersion relative to NFO and EBTSO.
Force-strain relations were fitted at 1 mm/s at three positions on each of three breast phantoms.
Variable desired-force control attained confidence comparable to higher constant-force references while using lower contact force.
Online FEM path correction, clinical validation, and broader manipulator transfer remain future work.

boundary_conditions: Force-strain fitting was quasi-static at 1 mm/s and did not identify relaxation or hysteresis.
The controller regulates desired force rather than impedance gains under force, passivity, or energy constraints.
No clinical generalization or alternative contact-model comparison was performed.
assumptions: A static local force-strain relation remains informative along the path.
Image confidence is a useful online force-update signal.
Phantom behavior is representative enough for concept validation.
Lower force at comparable confidence is a useful comfort/deformation proxy.

reported: Image-confidence-only control may not stabilize force.
Excessive force may cause discomfort and deformation.
Deformation-induced path error, clinical robustness, and broader generalization remain unresolved.
inferred: Static regression may fail under rate dependence, relaxation, hysteresis, or changing contact area.
The study cannot separate gains from path smoothing, model adequacy, and feedback correction.
Comparable confidence does not establish peak-force bounds, passivity, robustness, or impedance optimality.

conflicts_with: A blanket claim that continuous soft scanning necessarily requires a richer memory or pressure-field model.
A claim that static force-strain regression is sufficient for general optimal impedance control.

problem_lead_search_contexts.lead_statement: For continuous robotic ultrasound scanning, extending NNBO beyond a scalar normal Hunt-Crossley environment may be necessary because finite-area sliding, changing surface geometry, tangential resistance, and contact moment can alter the impedance decision and its safety/performance boundary.
problem_lead_search_contexts.purpose: Attempt to falsify the claim that the scalar normal Hunt-Crossley environment representation is insufficient for force- and trajectory-relevant sliding ultrasound contact by locating direct models and experiments that already close the finite-area, tangential-force, and contact-moment gap.
problem_lead_search_contexts.expected_close_condition: Identify direct robotic-ultrasound evidence showing whether finite-area geometry, sliding resistance, or contact moment materially changes force regulation or scanning behavior, or conclude that the claimed phenomenon lacks decision-grade support.

problem_lead_search_contexts.lead_statement: For continuous robotic ultrasound scanning, extending NNBO beyond a scalar normal Hunt-Crossley environment may be necessary because finite-area sliding, changing surface geometry, tangential resistance, and contact moment can alter the impedance decision and its safety/performance boundary.
problem_lead_search_contexts.purpose: Check the closest ultrasound force-regulation route for evidence that geometry/deformation-aware desired-force adaptation or path planning already removes the need for a richer environment model in optimal impedance selection.
problem_lead_search_contexts.expected_close_condition: Determine the overlap and residual delta between geometry/deformation-aware ultrasound force regulation and the proposed environment-model-dependent optimal impedance question.
